correctness.rationale: The polar equations give R'=2λ/ω+(2σ/ω+2β cos(2θ))R in the lifted angle. W=R/F stays positive at every finite forward angle and satisfies dW/dt=2λW. Its endpoint is finite positive exactly for σ>0; there R diverges as F grows, so the inverse clock gives the maximal physical time. For σ<0, the past-tail particular solution is positive and periodic, and every radial difference is a multiple of F tending to zero. The one-period Laplace sum is I₀(β)/ε+O(1) uniformly in phase, giving both stated threshold constants. At σ=0, the primitive of the periodic integrand is I₀(β)θ+O(1); the exact W law gives the angular coefficient, and the unbounded angle forbids convergence of the oscillating rescaled radius. For σ>0, with u=1−W/W∞, (T−t)R/P=(1−u)(−log(1−u))/u→1. P'=(2σ/ω+2β cos(2θ))P−1/ω rules out constancy for κ≠0, and each phase is attained indefinitely.
